Commentary on His saying, exalted is He:

[40:5] ﴿Before them the people of Noah denied, and the factions after them. And every nation plotted against their messenger to seize him, and they argued with falsehood in order to refute by it the truth. So I seized them, and how was My retribution!﴾

﴿The people of Noah denied before them, and the factions﴾ means: those who formed factions against the messengers and opposed them. ﴿After them﴾ means: after hearing their reports and witnessing their traces. ﴿And every nation plotted against their messenger to seize him﴾ means: to gain power over him, to bring harm upon him, and to inflict on him what they wished of torment or killing. Here "seize" (akhadha) carries the sense of capture, and "al-akhid" means the captive, the prisoner. ﴿And they argued with falsehood﴾ means: they met the arguments of the messengers with falsehood in their disputing. ﴿In order to refute by it the truth﴾ means: in order to remove by it the matter that is established by sound proof. Yet it will not be refuted, however many the doubts become, because it is the truth in itself, firmly established by its own essence. ﴿So I seized them﴾ means: with the worldly punishment whose reports are known and whose traces are witnessed. ﴿And how was My retribution!﴾ means: in this world; thus by it one takes warning, and so too the retribution of that abode (the Hereafter).

﴿Thus has the word of your Lord been justified against those who disbelieved, that they are the companions of the Fire.﴾ Ibn Jarir said: That is, just as it was decreed against the nations that denied their messengers, whose stories I have related to you, O Muhammad, and upon whom My punishment descended, so too the word of your Lord has become binding against those among your people who disbelieved in Allah, those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah, because they are the companions of the Fire.

(p-5157) On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[7–10] ﴿Those who bear the Throne and those around it glorify their Lord with His praise and believe in Him, and they ask forgiveness for those who believe: "Our Lord, You encompass all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who repent and follow Your way, and protect them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire."﴾ ﴿"Our Lord, and admit them to gardens of perpetual residence which You have promised them, along with whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their offspring. Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise."﴾ [Ghafir: 8] ﴿"And protect them from evil deeds. And whoever You protect from evil deeds that Day, You have had mercy upon him. And that is the great triumph."﴾ [Ghafir: 9] ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved will be called out to: "The aversion of Allah towards you is greater than your aversion towards yourselves, when you were being called to faith but you disbelieved."﴾ [Ghafir: 10]

﴿Those who bear the Throne﴾ means: of the angels. The discussion concerning the bearers of the Throne has already preceded in the commentary on the verse: ﴿Then He established Himself over the Throne﴾ [Al-A'raf: 54] in Surat al-A'raf, so refer back to it.

﴿And those around it﴾ means: the angels brought near (al-muqarrabin): ﴿glorify their Lord with His praise and believe in Him﴾, that is, they affirm that there is no deity for them besides Him, and they bear witness to that, not being arrogant about His worship. [11] ﴿They will say, "Our Lord, You have made us die twice and You have given us life twice, and we have acknowledged our sins, so is there any way to get out?"﴾

﴿They will say, "Our Lord, You have made us die twice and You have given us life twice"﴾ That is: You brought us into being as dead twice, and You gave us life in both creations, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿You were dead and He gave you life; then He will cause you to die, then He will bring you to life again﴾ [al-Baqarah: 28]. Al-Zamakhshari said: This is the speech of one overcome by despair and hopelessness, and they say this only as an excuse and in bewilderment. Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 40, verses 12–13:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[12, 13] ﴿That is because when Allah alone was invoked, you disbelieved; but when partners were associated with Him, you believed. So judgment belongs to Allah, the Most High, the Greatest.﴾ ﴿It is He who shows you His signs and sends down for you provision from the sky. And none remembers except one who turns back (in repentance).﴾ [Ghafir: 13].

﴿That﴾, i.e., that which you are in of punishment, and that there is no way out ever: ﴿because when Allah alone was invoked, you disbelieved; but when partners were associated with Him, you believed﴾, i.e., because of your denial that divinity belongs to Him exclusively, and your saying: ﴿Has he made the gods into one God? Indeed, this is a strange thing!﴾ [Sad: 5], and your belief in association: ﴿So judgment belongs to Allah, the Most High, the Greatest﴾, i.e., the decision belongs to Him alone, not to another. There is no way to salvation because of His exaltedness and His greatness, and it is impossible for anyone to reject His wisdom and His punishment. ﴿It is He who shows you His signs﴾ [Ghafir: 13], i.e., from the wind, the clouds, the thunder, the lightning, the thunderbolts, and the like. ﴿And sends down for you provision from the sky﴾ [Ghafir: 13], i.e., rain. Its being singled out for mention among the signs is because of the greatness of its benefit and because the life of every thing is caused by it. ﴿And none remembers except one who turns back (in repentance)﴾ [Ghafir: 13], i.e., none takes heed of His signs, exalted is He, except one who returns to Him in repentance and penitence.

[14, 15] ﴿So call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion, even if the disbelievers dislike it.﴾ ﴿Raised in degrees, Owner of the Throne, He casts the Spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants, that He may warn of the Day of Meeting.﴾ [Ghafir: 15].

The discourse on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[28] ﴿And a believing man from among the family of Pharaoh, who concealed his faith, said: "Will you kill a man because he says, 'My Lord is Allah,' when he has brought you clear proofs from your Lord? And if he is a liar, upon him is his lie; but if he is truthful, some of what he promises you will afflict you. Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a transgressor and a liar."﴾.

﴿And a believing man from among the family of Pharaoh, who concealed his faith﴾, meaning: from among Pharaoh and his chiefs. ﴿"Will you kill a man because he says, 'My Lord is Allah,' when he has brought you clear proofs from your Lord? And if he is a liar, upon him is his lie; but if he is truthful, some of what he promises you will afflict you"﴾, meaning: of the punishment of this world, if you oppose him. Al-Zamakhshari (d. 538 AH) has pointed out the subtleties and secrets contained within this statement, summarized as follows: This believer led them on gradually toward faith by citing the sincerity of Moses, peace be upon him, through the fact that he brought them proofs from the One to whom lordship is attributed, several proofs and not just a single proof, and he expressed them in the definite form, meaning: the great proofs which you have witnessed and recognized as such, so that by this he might soften their stubbornness and break their fury.

Then he took them to task through argument by division, saying: He is either truthful or a liar. If he is a liar, the harm of his lie returns upon him. Or if he is truthful, then, if you oppose him, some of what he promises you will afflict you. He mentioned "some" (ba'd), on the assumption that he is a truthful prophet, whereas a prophet is truthful in all that he promises; because he followed with them the path of counsel and gentle dealing, and so he brought what was closer to their acceptance and more likely to win their assent, so that they would listen to him and not reject his truthfulness. For when he assumed him to be truthful, he had already affirmed that he is truthful in all that he promises. But he added: ﴿some of what he promises you will afflict you﴾ in order to diminish a part of his right in the outward wording of the speech, so as to show them that he is not speaking as one who gives him his due and praises him, let alone as one who is partisan for him. The placing of the liar before the truthful one is of this kind.

Al-Nasir (Ibn al-Munayyir) said: The placing of the liar before the truthful one here is in keeping with the statement of the Exalted: ﴿And a witness from among her family testified: "If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth, and he is among the liars." And if his shirt is torn from the back, then she has lied, and he is among the truthful﴾ [Yusuf: 26-27]. There the witness placed the sign of her truthfulness before the sign of Joseph's truthfulness, though the truthful one was Joseph, to remove suspicion and dispel doubt, and out of confidence that the truth was with him, and delay does not harm him for this purpose. Close to this kind of treatment for dispelling suspicion is what occurs in the story of Joseph with his brother, when he began with their bags before the bag of his brother. End of quotation.

﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a transgressor and a liar﴾. Al-Zamakhshari said: It is possible that if he were a transgressor and a liar, Allah would forsake him and destroy him, and his affair would not be set right, so that you would be rid of him; and that if he were a transgressor and a liar, Allah would not have guided him to prophethood, nor would He have strengthened him with the clear proofs.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[29] ﴿O my people, the kingdom is yours today, prevailing in the land. But who would help us against the might of Allah if it came upon us?﴾ Pharaoh said, ﴿I only show you what I see, and I only guide you to the path of rectitude.﴾ (p-5165)

﴿O my people, the kingdom is yours today, prevailing in the land﴾: that is, exalted and dominant. So do not ruin your affair against yourselves by your own hands, and do not expose us to His punishment.

﴿But who would help us against the might of Allah if it came upon us?﴾ Pharaoh said, ﴿I only show you what I see﴾: that is, I only advise you with what I find right regarding killing him (Moses). For the heavenly might coming because of his killing is a supposed matter, so following him is an error.

﴿And I only guide you﴾: that is, by presenting the opinion of killing him, ﴿to the path of rectitude﴾, which is averting the changing of your religion and the spreading of corruption in the land by spreading its laws.

[32] ﴿And O my people, indeed I fear for you the Day of Calling Out﴾.

﴿And O my people, indeed I fear for you the Day of Calling Out﴾ means the Day of Resurrection, i.e., its punishment. The discourse on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[34] ﴿And Joseph certainly came to you before with clear proofs, but you remained in doubt about what he brought you. Then, when he died, you said, "Allah will never send after him any messenger." Thus does Allah leave astray whoever is a transgressor and a doubter.﴾

﴿And Joseph certainly came to you before with clear proofs﴾ That is, before the coming of Moses with the evident arguments (p-5167) and the luminous proofs, establishing the obligation of worshipping Him alone. Like His saying: ﴿Are lords divided among themselves better, or Allah, the One, the Subduer?﴾ [Yusuf: 39]. ﴿But you remained in doubt about what he brought you﴾ That is, despite the manifest uprightness of his conduct, which was sufficient as evidence for the truth of what he brought you. So you pronounced a judgment from yourselves, that Allah would not send a messenger, while doubting the sending of the one who had been given the clear proofs, out of the extremity of your misguidance. ﴿Thus does Allah leave astray whoever is a transgressor﴾ That is, in casting doubt when the decisive proofs have become manifest. ﴿a doubter﴾ That is, one who is in doubt despite the signs of certainty being apparent.

[35] ﴿Those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without any authority having come to them—it is greatly hateful in the sight of Allah and in the sight of those who believe. Thus does Allah seal every heart of an arrogant, tyrannical person.﴾.

﴿Those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without any authority﴾ i.e., without proof, ﴿having come to them—it is greatly hateful in the sight of Allah and in the sight of those who believe. Thus does Allah seal every heart of an arrogant, tyrannical person﴾ i.e., one who is insolent toward the truth, who does not accept proof, tyrannical in disputation, and stubborn. From him there issue the like of what has been mentioned: excess, doubt, and disputing falsehood in order to obliterate his insight, so that the truth can hardly appear to him.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 40, verses 43–44:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[43, 44] ﴿There is no doubt that what you call me to has no call (to it) in this world or in the Hereafter, and that our return is to Allah, and that the transgressors are the companions of the Fire. So you will remember what I say to you, and I entrust my affair to Allah. Indeed, Allah is Seeing of (His) servants.﴾ [Ghafir: 44].

﴿There is no doubt that what you call me to has no call (to it) in this world or in the Hereafter﴾ That is, the one to whose worship you call me has no call in this world to remove hardships, illnesses and the like, (p-5170) nor in the Hereafter to remove its terrors, according to what al-Mahayimi said. Or: it has no call in either abode because of its own non-existence and the impossibility of its existing in them, according to what al-Qashani said. Al-Shihab said: the absence of a call is an expression of its being inanimate and its not deserving that.

The construction of "la jarama" (لا جَرَمَ) according to the Basrans is that "la" is a refutation of what his people called him to, and "jarama" means "earned"; that is, their calling him to it earned the invalidity of his call, meaning that nothing resulted from that except the manifestation of the invalidity of his call. It is also possible that "la jarama" is like "la budda" (لابُدَّ) from "al-jarm," which is cutting. Just as you say, "la budda laka an taf'ala" (you must do such-and-such). "Al-budd" derives from "al-tabdid," which is separation, and its meaning is: there is no separation for you from doing such-and-such. Likewise, "la jarama" means there is no cessation to the invalidity of the call of the idols; rather, it is invalid forever. This is what is derived from al-Kashshaf.

In al-Sihah, al-Farra' said: "la jarama" was originally a phrase with the status of "la mahala" and "la budda," so it went that way and became common, until it transformed into the meaning of an oath, and came to have the status of "haqqan," which is why it is answered with the lam. Do you not see them saying: "la jarama la-ata'naka" (there is no doubt that we came to you)? Ibn Hisham in al-Mughni investigated the matter in a discussion, and al-Jalal in Hama'i' al-Hawami, during the discussion of "inna" and the oath; so consult both of them.

﴿And that our return is to Allah, and that the transgressors﴾ That is, in error, transgression, and shedding blood: ﴿are the companions of the Fire.﴾ ﴿So you will remember what I say to you﴾ [Ghafir: 44] That is, in the advice when the terrors are witnessed and what will befall you: ﴿and I entrust my affair to Allah﴾ [Ghafir: 44] That is, I surrender my affair to Him, make it to Him, and rely upon Him, for He is sufficient for whoever relies upon Him: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Seeing of (His) servants﴾ [Ghafir: 44] That is, He knows the obedient among them, the disobedient, and who deserves reward and punishment.

[45] ﴿So Allah protected him from the evils of what they plotted, and there befell the people of Pharaoh the worst of punishment.﴾

﴿So Allah protected him from the evils of what they plotted﴾: that is, Allah lifted from this believing man of the family of Pharaoh, because of his faith and his affirmation of His Messenger Musa (Moses), the harm of the punishment and trial with which Pharaoh used to afflict those who opposed him, and He saved him from it. ﴿And there befell the people of Pharaoh﴾: that is, Pharaoh and his people. ﴿The worst of punishment﴾: meaning drowning, or the Fire. According to the first interpretation, the words of His Exalted saying:

(p-5171) The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[46–48] ﴿The Fire; they are exposed to it morning and evening. And on the Day the Hour is established: "Admit the people of Pharaoh into the severest punishment."﴾ ﴿And when they argue with one another in the Fire, the weak will say to those who were arrogant: "Indeed, we were your followers, so will you relieve us of some portion of the Fire?"﴾ [Ghafir: 47] ﴿Those who were arrogant will say: "Indeed, we are all in it. Indeed, Allah has already judged between the servants."﴾ [Ghafir: 48].

﴿The Fire; they are exposed to it morning and evening﴾ is a resumptive sentence (jumlah musta'nafah) explaining the manner in which the punishment descends upon them. It may be read as follows: {The Fire} is the subject (mubtada'), and the clause {they are exposed to it} (yu'radun) is its predicate (khabar). According to the second reading, {the Fire} is the predicate of an omitted subject, namely the predicate of "the evil punishment," or it is a substitute (badal) for {the evil of the punishment}. What is meant is that their souls are exposed to it continually. He suffices with the two encompassing extremes, the morning and the evening, to stand for the whole, and from this the proof for the punishment of the grave (adhab al-qabr) and the intermediate state (al-barzakh) is derived. May Allah, by His favor, protect us.

Al-Suyuti said: In (al-'Aja'ib) of al-Karmani, the verse is the clearest proof for the punishment of the grave, because the conjoined element is other than that to which it is conjoined. He means His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and on the Day the Hour is established﴾, meaning: this exposure lasts as long as the world endures. When the Hour is established, it will be said to them: ﴿Admit the people of Pharaoh into the severest punishment﴾, which is the punishment of Jahannam, because it is the recompense for the severity of their disbelief. ﴿And when they argue with one another in the Fire﴾ [Ghafir: 47], meaning: they dispute therein, the followers and those who were followed. ﴿The weak will say to those who were arrogant: "Indeed, we were your followers"﴾ [Ghafir: 47], meaning: followers like those who were compelled. ﴿So will you relieve us of some portion of the Fire?﴾ [Ghafir: 47] ﴿Those who were arrogant will say: "Indeed, we are all in it"﴾ [Ghafir: 48], meaning: we and you. Or it means: by decreeing for each of us a punishment that cannot be repelled from him and that no one else can bear on his behalf. Al-Shihab said: This is more fitting with what precedes it.

(p-5171) The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[46–48] ﴿The Fire; they are exposed to it morning and evening. And on the Day the Hour is established: "Admit the people of Pharaoh into the severest punishment."﴾ ﴿And when they argue with one another in the Fire, the weak will say to those who were arrogant: "Indeed, we were your followers, so will you relieve us of some portion of the Fire?"﴾ [Ghafir: 47] ﴿Those who were arrogant will say: "Indeed, we are all in it. Indeed, Allah has already judged between the servants."﴾ [Ghafir: 48].

﴿The Fire; they are exposed to it morning and evening﴾ is a resumptive sentence (jumlah musta'nafah) explaining the manner in which the punishment descends upon them. It may be read as follows: {The Fire} is the subject (mubtada'), and the clause {they are exposed to it} (yu'radun) is its predicate (khabar). According to the second reading, {the Fire} is the predicate of an omitted subject, namely the predicate of "the evil punishment," or it is a substitute (badal) for {the evil of the punishment}. What is meant is that their souls are exposed to it continually. He suffices with the two encompassing extremes, the morning and the evening, to stand for the whole, and from this the proof for the punishment of the grave (adhab al-qabr) and the intermediate state (al-barzakh) is derived. May Allah, by His favor, protect us.

Al-Suyuti said: In (al-'Aja'ib) of al-Karmani, the verse is the clearest proof for the punishment of the grave, because the conjoined element is other than that to which it is conjoined. He means His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and on the Day the Hour is established﴾, meaning: this exposure lasts as long as the world endures. When the Hour is established, it will be said to them: ﴿Admit the people of Pharaoh into the severest punishment﴾, which is the punishment of Jahannam, because it is the recompense for the severity of their disbelief. ﴿And when they argue with one another in the Fire﴾ [Ghafir: 47], meaning: they dispute therein, the followers and those who were followed. ﴿The weak will say to those who were arrogant: "Indeed, we were your followers"﴾ [Ghafir: 47], meaning: followers like those who were compelled. ﴿So will you relieve us of some portion of the Fire?﴾ [Ghafir: 47] ﴿Those who were arrogant will say: "Indeed, we are all in it"﴾ [Ghafir: 48], meaning: we and you. How could we relieve you? Had we been able, we would have relieved ourselves. ﴿Indeed, Allah has already judged between the servants﴾ [Ghafir: 48], meaning: by admitting the people of Paradise to Paradise and the people of the Fire to the Fire, and none can avert His judgment. Or it means: by decreeing for each of us a punishment that cannot be repelled from him and that no one else can bear on his behalf. Al-Shihab said: This is more fitting with what precedes it.

**Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 40, verse 49:**

(p-5172) The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[49] ﴿And those in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell, "Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment."﴾

﴿And those in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell﴾ That is, when they despaired of any lightening through argument: ﴿"Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment."﴾ That is, to ward off from us a day of the days of punishment, or the pain of a day and its severity.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[50] ﴿They say: "Did not your messengers come to you with clear proofs?" They say: "Yes." They say: "Then call upon [them]. But the supplication of the disbelievers is only in error."﴾

﴿They say: "Did not your messengers come to you with clear proofs?"﴾ That is, proofs that were abundant in attesting to their truthfulness, and that warned of this severe punishment. ﴿They say: "Yes."﴾ That is, they came with them, and informed [you] along with the clear proofs. ﴿They say: "Then call upon [them]."﴾ That is, if it will benefit you. And how far-fetched [it is]: ﴿But the supplication of the disbelievers is only in error.﴾ That is, in a loss that receives no answer.

The Discourse on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[51] ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who believe, in the life of this world and on the day when the witnesses stand up.﴾

﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who believe, in the life of this world and on the day when the witnesses stand up.﴾ That is: We shall support them in both abodes. As for in this world, it is by destroying their enemy and annihilating him swiftly, or by granting them victory over their enemy and making them dominant over him, giving them ascendancy (dawla) and well-being for their followers. As for in the Hereafter, it is by everlasting bliss and perpetual joy. And: {al-ashhad} (the witnesses) is the plural of shahid (witness), and they are those who bear witness to the messengers' conveying of the message and to their being denied unjustly; or it is the plural of shahid (martyr/witness), like ashraf (nobles) and sharif (noble).

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[52] ﴿On the Day when their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers, and for them is the curse, and for them is the evil abode.﴾

﴿On the Day when their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers, and for them is the curse, and for them is the evil abode.﴾ Ibn Jarir said: That is a Day on which the excuse of the people of *shirk* (associating partners with God) will not benefit them, because they offer no excuse except with falsehood. That is because God had already given them an excuse in the world, and had followed up the proofs against them therein, so they have no argument in the Hereafter except clinging to lies, by saying: ﴿By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ [al-An'am: 23]. Therefore they have the curse, which is distance from the mercy of God, and the worst of what is in the abode of the Hereafter, of painful punishment.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[53] ﴿And We certainly gave Moses the guidance, and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit the Book﴾.

﴿And We certainly gave Moses the guidance﴾ i.e., that by which one is guided. Pharaoh and his people denied it, just as the Quraysh denied (the Prophet ﷺ). ﴿And We caused the Children of Israel to inherit the Book﴾ i.e., We left them after him, from that, the Torah.

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[54] ﴿A guidance and a reminder for people of understanding.﴾

﴿Guidance﴾ means: a clarification concerning the matter of their religion, and of the laws (sharai') of it which We obligated upon them. ﴿And a reminder for people of understanding﴾ means: for those among them who possess intellect (hijā) and reason (ʿuqūl).

Commentary on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[55] ﴿So be patient; indeed, the promise of Allah is true. And ask forgiveness for your sin, and glorify the praise of your Lord in the evening and the morning.﴾

﴿So be patient﴾ means: when you recite to the people what We have related to you, then be patient over the harm of the polytheists, and proclaim openly what you are commanded. ﴿Indeed, the promise of Allah is true﴾ means: [that is, the promise of] His victory for you over whoever opposed you; there is no breaking of it, and He will fulfil it. And mention the account of Musa and Fir'awn. ﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin﴾ means: ask Him for His forgiveness and His pardon. ﴿And glorify the praise of your Lord in the evening and the morning﴾, like His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And glorify the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting﴾ [Qaf: 39].

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[56] ﴿Indeed, those who dispute about the signs of Allah without any authority having come to them—there is nothing in their breasts but pride, which they will never attain. So seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.﴾

﴿Indeed, those who dispute about the signs of Allah without any authority having come to them﴾ means: they repel the truth with falsehood, and they refute sound proofs with corrupt doubts, without any demonstration or proof from Allah. ﴿There is nothing in their breasts but pride﴾ means: nothing but arrogance toward the truth, and self-exaltation that refuses to reflect, and denial of the one who brought it to them, out of envy toward the bounty that Allah has given you and the honor with which He has favored you through prophethood. ﴿Which they will never attain﴾: Ibn Jarir said: that is, the thing they envy you for is something they will never reach or obtain, because that is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whomever He wills, and it is not a matter that is attained through wishful thinking. It has also been said that its meaning is: there is nothing in their breasts but greatness, which they will never attain, because Allah will humiliate them. ﴿So seek refuge in Allah﴾: Ibn Jarir (p. 5175) said: that is, seek protection in Allah, O Muhammad, from the evil of these people who dispute about the signs of Allah without any authority, and from the pride that might arise in your heart. ﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾ means: of what they say and of what they do, and so He will requite them.

Note:

Ka'b and Abu al-'Aliyah said: "This verse was revealed concerning the Jews, because they claimed that the Dajjal (the Antichrist) was from among them, and that by him they would rule the earth. So the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to seek refuge in Allah from his trial." Ibn Kathir said: This is a strange statement, and it contains a far-fetched interpretation. Even though Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it, Ibn Jarir did not mention it, despite his fondness for the strange and the weak.

In al-Iklil, it is said: The Qur'an contains no allusion to the Dajjal except in this verse, that is, if this narration is authentic.

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[57] ﴿Indeed, the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most of mankind do not know.﴾

﴿Indeed, the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind﴾ — i.e., their origination and bringing into being from nothing is greater than the creation of human beings. ﴿But most of mankind do not know﴾ — i.e., they do not reflect or contemplate, due to the dominance of ignorance over them; therefore they consider the re-creation of a thing to be greater than its creation out of nothing, even though it is easier and less difficult.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 40, verse 58:

The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[58] ﴿And the blind and the seeing are not equal, nor are those who believe and do righteous deeds and the wrongdoer. Little do you remember.﴾

﴿And the blind and the seeing are not equal﴾ meaning: the blind man who sees nothing is not equal to the one who sees. The blind man is a parable for the disbeliever who does not contemplate God's proofs (hujaj) with his eyes, so that he reflects upon them and takes lessons from them, and thus knows His oneness and His power to create whatever He wills, and believes in Him. The seeing man, who sees with his eyes what is set before them and perceives it, is a parable for the believer who sees God's proofs with his eyes, reflects upon them, takes admonition, and knows what they indicate of the oneness of their Creator and the greatness of His dominion. ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ meaning: nor are the believers in God and His Messenger, who obey their Lord, equal [to the wrongdoer]. ﴿Nor the wrongdoer﴾, who is the disbeliever in his Lord, who disobeys Him and opposes His command. ﴿Little do you remember﴾ meaning: His proofs, exalted is He, so that they might take heed and be admonished; that is, if they had remembered His signs and taken lessons from them, they would have recognized the error of what they persist in, namely denying the Resurrection and the ugliness of polytheism.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[59] ﴿Indeed, the Hour is coming, there is no doubt about it, but most of the people do not believe.﴾

﴿Indeed, the Hour is coming, there is no doubt about it.﴾ I.e., be certain of its coming, and that you will be resurrected and recompensed for your deeds, so repent. ﴿But most of the people do not believe.﴾ I.e., they do not affirm its coming; meaning the polytheists.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[60] ﴿And your Lord says: "Call upon Me; I will respond to you. Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell, humbled."﴾

﴿And your Lord says: Call upon Me, I will respond to you﴾, that is: worship Me, and I will reward you. Al-Zamakhshari said: The word "supplication" (du'a') used in the sense of "worship" ('ibada) is common in the Qur'an, and His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell, humbled﴾, indicates this, meaning: abased and humiliated. Al-Shihab said: Applying "supplication" to "worship" is a metaphor (majaz), because worship includes supplication, since supplication is a specific form of worship, and the general is intended by the specific. Making "reward" (ithaba) the consequence of worship is called "response" (istijaba), a metaphor or a figurative correspondence (musha-akala). It was interpreted this way because what follows it indicates it, and the context fits it, namely the command to worship. (p-5177) It has also been permitted that "supplication" and "response" be understood in their apparent meanings, and that "worship" be understood as supplication metaphorically, because supplication is a great branch of worship and a splendid individual instance of it. Al-Shihab said: If it were said that there is no need for metaphor, because the idafa (genitive construction) here is intended to refer to a known (specific) reference, which conveys what has been mentioned without metaphor, it would be better. End of quotation.

On the second interpretation, namely that "supplication" means asking, many commentators limited themselves to this. Al-Mahayimi said: ﴿I will respond to you﴾, because supplication from the servant is the utmost expression of humbling himself before his Lord, and it is beloved to his Lord. So when the servant performs what is beloved to the Lord, He honors him by responding; and if He does not respond to him in this world, He compensates him in the Hereafter. Because He loves humility, He commanded the servants to worship, so if they are too proud, they will receive the utmost degradation. Al-Qashani said: The verse concerns the supplication of states (du'a' al-hal), because supplication by the tongue, without knowing whether what is asked for is good for one or not, is the supplication of the veiled ones. As for the supplication that response never fails to accompany, it is the supplication of the state, by which the servant prepares his readiness to receive what he seeks, and response does not fail to follow this supplication, like one who seeks forgiveness, repents to God, and turns back to Him through asceticism and obedience. End of quotation.

It has already been mentioned, under the verse ﴿I respond to the prayer of the supplicant when he calls upon Me﴾ [al-Baqara: 186], benefits that suit this context, so let them be consulted. Then He, exalted is He, pointed out how it is not necessary for the servants to worship Him, since He has bestowed upon them blessings that demand their gratitude through worship, among which He made clear the benefits of the night and the day, by His saying, glorified is He:

Commentary on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[61, 62] ﴿It is Allah who made the night for you that you may rest therein, and the day giving sight. Indeed, Allah is full of bounty to mankind, but most of mankind do not give thanks.﴾ ﴿That is Allah, your Lord, the Creator of all things. There is no deity except Him, so how are you turned away?﴾ [Ghafir: 62]

﴿It is Allah who made the night for you that you may rest therein﴾ That is: Allah is the One for whom divinity alone is fitting, and to whom alone worship is due, and He is the One who made the night dark for you that you may rest therein, so that you may recover in it the strength you lost in working by day. ﴿And the day giving sight﴾ meaning, in which things are seen, or by means of which, so that you may move about to obtain religious and worldly gains. Allah has bestowed upon you these two and what is in them as a favour.

﴿Indeed, Allah is full of bounty to mankind﴾ meaning, so that they may thank Him by worshipping Him: ﴿but most of mankind do not give thanks.﴾ ﴿That is Allah, your Lord, the Creator of all things. There is no deity except Him, so how are you turned away?﴾ [Ghafir: 62] meaning: away from His obedience towards affirming a partner and worshipping him.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[63] ﴿Thus are turned away those who used to deny the signs of Allah.﴾

﴿Thus are turned away those who used to deny the signs of Allah﴾: That is, from the earlier destroyed nations; meaning, you, O assembly of Quraysh, have followed their path and taken up their course into misguidance.

The Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on Surah 40, Verse 64:

The discussion of the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, Exalted is He:

[64] ﴿It is Allah who made the earth a place of settlement for you, and the sky a canopy, and fashioned you and perfected your forms, and provided you with good things. That is Allah, your Lord. So blessed is Allah, the Lord of the worlds.﴾

﴿It is Allah who made the earth a place of settlement for you﴾, i.e., you settle upon it and dwell above it. ﴿And the sky a canopy﴾, i.e., built and raised above you without pillars that you can see, for your benefit and for the sustenance of your worldly life. The word (bina', building) has been explained as a pitched dome, because the Arabs call tents (abniyah, buildings).

This is an eloquent metaphor, and it points to its roundness. Al-Shihab said: ﴿And fashioned you and perfected your forms﴾, i.e., He placed each limb in a place suited to it, so that its benefit is complete, and thereby you may infer from this the perfection of His wisdom. ﴿And provided you with good things﴾, i.e., delicious foods and drinks, so that you may give thanks to Him alone. ﴿That is Allah, your Lord. So blessed is Allah, the Lord of the worlds﴾, i.e., the One to whom alone lordship is fitting.

(p-5179) On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[65] ﴿He is the Ever-Living; there is no deity except Him, so invoke Him, sincere to Him in religion. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾

﴿He is the Ever-Living﴾, i.e., the One who does not die, the One whose life is everlasting. Everything other than Him has a life that is cut off and not everlasting. ﴿There is no deity except Him, so invoke Him, sincere to Him in religion﴾, i.e., singling Him out with obedience, not associating anything with Him in His worship. ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, i.e., praise and thanks belong to Allah, the Owner of all kinds of creation, not to the idols, which own nothing and have no power to harm or benefit.

Ibn Jarir said: A group of the people of knowledge used to instruct whoever says "There is no deity but Allah" to follow it with ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, taking this verse as a command from Allah to say that. He traced this back (to them) through a chain of narration from Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Jubayr.

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:

[66] ﴿Say: Indeed, I have been forbidden to worship those whom you invoke besides Allah, when the clear proofs have come to me from my Lord, and I have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds.﴾

﴿Say: Indeed, I have been forbidden to worship those whom you invoke besides Allah﴾ — that is, from among the deities and idols. ﴿when the clear proofs have come to me from my Lord﴾ — that is, the manifest signs from Him, indicating the obligation of His oneness and His being singled out for worship. ﴿and I have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds﴾ — that is, to humble myself to Him in obedience, to the exclusion of anything else.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[67] ﴿He is the One who created you from dust, then from a drop of fluid, then from a clinging clot, then He brings you forth as a child; then [He lets you live] that you may reach your full strength, then that you may become elders. Among you is one who is taken in death before that, so that you may reach a specified term, and perhaps you will use your reason.﴾

(p-٥١٨٠) ﴿He created you from dust﴾, i.e., from that to which you return. Or He created your father Adam from it. ﴿Then from a drop of fluid, then from a clinging clot, then He brings you forth as a child, then that you may reach your full strength﴾, i.e., He keeps you alive so that you reach your full strength, and your powers become complete. ﴿Then that you may become﴾, i.e., when your youth has ended and the completion of your creation is reached, ﴿elders. Among you is one who is taken in death before that﴾, i.e., before he becomes an elder. ﴿So that you may reach﴾, i.e., and We do that so that you reach ﴿a specified term﴾, i.e., a fixed appointed time for your lives, which is the time of death, or for your recompense, which is the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And perhaps you will use your reason﴾, i.e., so that you may understand the proofs of God against you through this, and reflect upon His signs, and thereby recognize that there is no god but Him.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 40, verse 68:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[68] ﴿He is the One who gives life and causes death. And when He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾

﴿He is the One who gives life and causes death. And when He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ That is: it comes into being without effort or toil. The discussion of this verse has already been given at length in (Surat al-Baqarah).

The commentary on His saying, Exalted is He:

[69–72] "Have you not considered those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah – how are they turned away? Those who denied the Book and that with which We sent Our messengers – they will soon know. When the shackles are around their necks and the chains, they are dragged. Into scalding water, then into the Fire they are kindled."

"Have you not considered those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah – how are they turned away?" That is: away from guidance toward error (p-5181).

"Those who denied the Book" [Ghafir: 70], meaning: the Book of Allah, which is the Qur'an; "and that with which We sent Our messengers – they will soon know" [Ghafir: 70]. "When the shackles are around their necks and the chains, they are dragged" [Ghafir: 71]. "Into scalding water" [Ghafir: 72], meaning: hot water. Al-Mahayimi said: because of their rejection of the cold certainty of the proofs of the Book and the Sunnah. "Then into the Fire they are kindled" [Ghafir: 72], meaning: they are burned. Al-Mahayimi said: because of their burning of the rational and transmitted proofs.

The discussion of the words of His exalted saying:

[73–74] ﴿Then it will be said to them, "Where are those you used to associate with﴾ ﴿besides Allah?" They will say, "They have vanished from us." Rather, we did not used to call upon anything before." Thus does Allah leave the disbelievers astray.﴾ [Ghafir: 74].

﴿Then it will be said to them, "Where are those you used to associate with﴾ ﴿besides Allah?" They will say, "They have vanished from us"﴾ [Ghafir: 74]: that is, they were absent, so we did not know their place. This [answer] comes before they are joined with them (the idols), or their "going astray" is a metaphor for their uselessness to them. The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[75] ﴿That is because you used to exult in the land without right, and because you used to be insolent.﴾

﴿That﴾ refers to the punishment: ﴿because you used to exult in the land without right, and because you used to be insolent﴾, i.e., because of your exultation in the world, in what is not permitted by God to you, from falsehood and sins, and because of your insolence therein. **The discussion of the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:**

[78] ﴿And We have certainly sent messengers before you. Among them are those whom We have related to you, and among them are those whom We have not related to you. And it was not for any messenger to bring a sign except by permission of Allah. So when the command of Allah comes, it will be concluded with truth, and the falsifiers will lose therein.﴾

﴿And We have certainly sent messengers before you. Among them are those whom We have related to you﴾, meaning: so that you would recognize what We fulfilled for them of the promise of victory over them in this world. ﴿And among them are those whom We have not related to you﴾, meaning: because of the length (of the account). Yet their story contains what resembles the stories of those mentioned, and a thing is judged by its likeness. ﴿And it was not for any messenger to bring a sign except by permission of Allah﴾ [(p-5183)], meaning: by His command. This is a rejection of their proposal and their obstinacy in seeking a sign other than what was related to them, such as Allah's words: ﴿And they say, "We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth"﴾ [al-Isra: 90], and so on. (The answer is that) bringing such a thing depends on the will of Allah, Exalted is He, and His desire for it. He has willed that the greatest sign be His revelation, the greatest of every sign and the most magnificent of every extraordinary event. It is therefore the best of the signs, the finest of them, the most upright of the miracles, and the firmest of them. As Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring a better one than it or like it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 106]. And He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book?﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 51].

﴿So when the command of Allah comes﴾, meaning: when the proposed sign is not believed in after it has come. ﴿It will be concluded with truth﴾, meaning: with the requital, after the proposed proof has been established for them. ﴿And the falsifiers will lose therein﴾, meaning: in their claim of a partner and their fabrication of falsehood.

The discussion on the interpretation of His, exalted is He, saying:

[83–85] ﴿So when their messengers came to them with clear proofs, they rejoiced in what knowledge they had, and there befell them what they used to mock.﴾ ﴿So when they saw Our might, they said, "We believe in Allah alone, and we disbelieve in what we used to associate with Him."﴾ [Ghafir: 84] ﴿But their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our might. This is the way of Allah which has already passed among His servants, and there the disbelievers were lost.﴾ [Ghafir: 85].

﴿So when their messengers came to them with clear proofs, they rejoiced in what knowledge they had﴾, i.e., the knowledge that was empty of the light of guidance and revelation. They were content with it and rejected accepting the guidance and teachings of the messengers. They mocked their messengers, considering them insignificant for what they brought, compared with the imaginary knowledge they possessed. ﴿And there befell them﴾, i.e., of the punishment of Allah, ﴿what they used to mock﴾, i.e., its recompense. ﴿So when they saw Our might, they said, "We believe in Allah alone, and we disbelieve in what we used to associate with Him."﴾ [Ghafir: 84] ﴿But their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our might. This is the way of Allah which has already passed among His servants﴾ [Ghafir: 85], i.e., it has gone on in His creation, that He does not accept repentance or faith in that state. ﴿And there the disbelievers were lost﴾ [Ghafir: 85], i.e., they perished at the coming of His might, the disbelievers in their Lord who denied the tawhid (affirmation of the oneness of God) of their Creator. Thus the happiness of eternity and the pleasant life escaped them.

We ask Him, exalted is He, for protection from His anger and His punishment, and for companionship with the company of His beloved. Amen.
